# Reshape wide & long

::: {.question}
**Which direction do you need to reshape?**

- [Wide to long (e.g. trial1, trial2, trial3 → one 'trial' column)](09-reshape.qmd#sec-reshape-long)
- [Long to wide (one row per trial → one row per participant)](09-reshape.qmd#sec-reshape-wide)
:::

## Reshape wide to long {#sec-reshape-long}

::: {.pkgs}
Packages: `tidyr`
:::

Long format — one row per observation — is what most repeated-measures ANOVAs and mixed-effects models in R expect.

```r
library(tidyr)

survey_long <- survey_raw |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("trial"),
    names_to = "trial",
    values_to = "rt"
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip}
`cols` accepts helpers like `starts_with()`, `contains()`, or just a plain vector of column names.
:::

::: {.next-steps}
**Where to next:**

- [Now check your data is clean](13-validate.qmd#sec-validate)
:::

## Reshape long to wide {#sec-reshape-wide}

::: {.pkgs}
Packages: `tidyr`
:::

Useful when you need one row per participant for a correlation matrix or a simple summary table.

```r
library(tidyr)

survey_wide <- survey_long |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = trial,
    values_from = rt
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip}
pivot_wider() and pivot_longer() are exact inverses — if something looks wrong, try reversing the operation to see where it breaks.
:::
